title: The Particulate Nature of Matter
seo_title: Secondary 3 Chemistry: The Particulate Nature of Matter Worksheets (O-Level 6092 with Answers)
standard_code: O-Level Chemistry (6092): The Particulate Nature of Matter
standard_text: Describe the solid, liquid and gaseous states of matter and changes of state in terms of the kinetic particle theory and the energy changes involved; describe and explain diffusion and the effect of molecular mass and temperature on its rate; state the relative charges and approximate relative masses of protons, neutrons and electrons; define proton (atomic) number and nucleon (mass) number and use nuclide notation; define isotopes; describe the build-up of electrons in shells for the first 20 elements (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Chemistry 6092 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Chemistry worksheets on the particulate nature of matter: kinetic particle theory, changes of state, diffusion, atomic structure, isotopes and electronic configuration. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Atoms: protons and neutrons in the nucleus, electrons in shells.
body_html:
How to think about it

Matter is made of particles; atoms are made of protons, neutrons and electrons.

  • Changes of state: particles gain or lose energy; the temperature stays constant while a pure substance melts or boils.
  • Diffusion is faster for lighter molecules and at higher temperature.
  • Proton +1 (mass 1), neutron 0 (mass 1), electron −1 (mass about 1/1840). Proton number Z; nucleon number A = protons + neutrons.
  • Isotopes: same Z, different numbers of neutrons. Electron shells hold 2, 8, 8 for the first 20 elements.
Example

Neutrons in ³⁷₁₇Cl?

37 − 17

Answer: 20

Example

Electronic configuration of aluminium (Z = 13)?

2 + 8 + 3

Answer: 2, 8, 3

Common mistakes

  • Calling the nucleon number the number of neutrons. It is protons + neutrons.
  • Saying isotopes have different numbers of protons.
  • Thinking heavier gas molecules diffuse faster.
  • Putting more than 2 electrons in the first shell.

faq.q: How do you find the number of neutrons?
faq.a: Subtract the proton number from the nucleon number: neutrons = A − Z.
Atoms of the same element (same number of protons) with different numbers of neutrons, so different nucleon numbers. They have the same chemical properties.

faq.q: How are electrons arranged in the first 20 elements?
faq.a: Up to 2 in the first shell, then up to 8 in the second and 8 in the third; calcium is 2, 8, 8, 2.

sets.title: States of matter and changes of state

items.q: Which gas diffuses faster at the same temperature: methane (relative mass 16) or carbon dioxide (relative mass 44)?
c: Both diffuse at the same rate.
items.e: Lighter particles move faster on average, so they diffuse faster.

items.q: What does the kinetic particle theory say about all matter?
c: It is made of particles that never move.
It is made of tiny particles in constant random motion.
It is continuous with no gaps.
items.e: The particles move faster at higher temperature.

items.q: Which change of state is this? “The particles of a solid gain enough energy to escape directly into the gas state.”
items.e: Sublimation: The particles of a solid gain enough energy to escape directly into the gas state.

items.q: Why does nitrogen diffuse faster than chlorine?
c: Its particles have a smaller mass, so they move faster at the same temperature.
Its particles are attracted to air.
Its particles have a larger mass.
items.e: Rate of diffusion falls as molecular mass rises.

items.q: Why does helium diffuse faster than ammonia?
c: Its particles have a larger mass.
Its particles have a smaller mass, so they move faster at the same temperature.
Its particles are attracted to air.
items.e: Rate of diffusion falls as molecular mass rises.

items.q: Which change of state is this? “The particles gain energy and vibrate so much that they break out of their fixed positions.”
items.e: Melting: The particles gain energy and vibrate so much that they break out of their fixed positions.

items.q: What are isotopes?
c: atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
atoms of different elements with the same mass
atoms with different numbers of protons
items.e: Same proton number, different nucleon numbers.

items.q: Which statement about the nucleus is correct?
c: It contains almost all the mass of the atom but is very small.
It is the largest part of the atom by volume.
items.e: Electrons have almost no mass.

items.q: Why is an atom electrically neutral?
c: It has equal numbers of protons and neutrons.
It has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
items.e: The charges cancel.

items.q: Which change of state is this? “The gas particles lose energy, slow down and come close together to form a liquid.”
items.e: Condensation: The gas particles lose energy, slow down and come close together to form a liquid.

items.q: Which description matches evaporation?
c: Particles with the most energy escape from the surface of the liquid below its boiling point.
The particles gain energy and vibrate so much that they break out of their fixed positions.
The particles gain enough energy to overcome the forces of attraction and escape as a gas throughout the liquid.
The gas particles lose energy, slow down and come close together to form a liquid.
items.e: Evaporation: Particles with the most energy escape from the surface of the liquid below its boiling point.

items.q: Element X has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 6. What is its proton number?
Why do noble gases such as argon not form ions easily?
c: Their outer shells are full, which is a stable arrangement.
items.e: Argon: 2, 8, 8.

items.q: An atom has 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 11 electrons. What is its nucleon number?
Why does the temperature stay constant while a pure solid melts?
c: The energy taken in is used to overcome the forces between particles.
items.e: This is why pure substances have sharp melting points.

items.q: Which change of state is this? “Particles with the most energy escape from the surface of the liquid below its boiling point.”
items.e: Evaporation: Particles with the most energy escape from the surface of the liquid below its boiling point.

items.q: Why does methane diffuse faster than hydrogen chloride?
c: Its particles are attracted to air.
Its particles have a smaller mass, so they move faster at the same temperature.
Its particles have a larger mass.
items.e: Rate of diffusion falls as molecular mass rises.

items.q: Which description matches sublimation?
c: The particles lose energy and settle into fixed positions in a regular arrangement.
The gas particles lose energy, slow down and come close together to form a liquid.
Particles with the most energy escape from the surface of the liquid below its boiling point.
The particles of a solid gain enough energy to escape directly into the gas state.
items.e: Sublimation: The particles of a solid gain enough energy to escape directly into the gas state.

items.q: Oxygen moves from the air in the lungs into the blood. What is the best explanation?
c: The particles were pushed by convection only.
Diffusion: oxygen moved from a higher to a lower concentration.
The water or air particles stopped moving.
The particles grew bigger and filled the space.
items.e: Particles are always moving randomly, so there is a net movement from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.

items.q: How does a nitrogen atom form the ion N<sup>3−</sup>?
items.e: Ions form by gaining or losing electrons.

items.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of sodium-25?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 25 − 11 = 14.

items.q: How does a lithium atom form the ion Li<sup>+</sup>?
items.e: Ions form by gaining or losing electrons.

items.q: How does a selenium atom form the ion Se<sup>2−</sup>?
items.e: Ions form by gaining or losing electrons.

items.q: An atom has 20 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: The number of protons decides the element.

items.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of lead-210?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 210 − 82 = 128.

items.q: How many neutrons are in <sup>79</sup><sub>35</sub>Br?
What is the relative mass of an electron?
items.e: Protons and neutrons have relative mass 1; an electron's is about 1/1840.

items.q: Where is a neutron found in an atom?
items.e: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons.

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of sulfur-34?
items.e: The atomic number (16) is the number of protons.

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of calcium-41?
items.e: The atomic number (20) is the number of protons.

items.q: An atom has 4 neutrons and 3 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: Use the protons (3), not the neutrons.

items.q: An atom has 2 protons and 2 neutrons. What is its mass number?
How many protons are in an atom of beryllium-10?

items.q: Which particle has a relative charge of 0?
items.e: Proton +1, neutron 0, electron −1.

items.q: What is the relative charge of a neutron?

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of silicon-27?

items.q: Which particle has a relative charge of −1?

items.q: An atom has 16 neutrons and 13 protons. Which element is it?

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of phosphorus (proton number 15)?
items.e: Fill the shells in order: 2 in the first, 8 in the second, 8 in the third. Phosphorus: 2, 8, 5.

items.q: How many more neutrons does <sup>7</sup><sub>3</sub>Li have than <sup>6</sup><sub>3</sub>Li?
items.e: Neutrons: 7 − 3 = 4 and 6 − 3 = 3; difference = 1.

items.q: <sup>12</sup><sub>6</sub>C and <sup>14</sup><sub>6</sub>C are isotopes. In what way are their atoms different?
c: They have different numbers of electrons.
They have different numbers of protons.
They have different numbers of neutrons.
items.e: Isotopes have the same proton number but different nucleon numbers; same electron configuration, so same chemical properties.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of chlorine (proton number 17)?
items.e: Fill the shells in order: 2 in the first, 8 in the second, 8 in the third. Chlorine: 2, 8, 7.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of argon (proton number 18)?
items.e: Fill the shells in order: 2 in the first, 8 in the second, 8 in the third. Argon: 2, 8, 8.

items.q: How many occupied electron shells does a potassium atom (proton number 19) have?
items.e: Configuration 2, 8, 8, 1: 4 shells.

items.q: <sup>24</sup><sub>12</sub>Mg and <sup>26</sup><sub>12</sub>Mg are isotopes. In what way are their atoms different?
c: They have different numbers of protons.

items.q: How many more neutrons does <sup>90</sup>Sr have than <sup>88</sup>Sr?

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of boron (proton number 5)?

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of silicon (proton number 14)?
items.e: Fill the shells in order: 2 in the first, 8 in the second, 8 in the third. Silicon: 2, 8, 4.

items.q: Which pair are isotopes of the same element?

items.q: How many more neutrons does <sup>26</sup><sub>12</sub>Mg have than <sup>24</sup><sub>12</sub>Mg?
items.e: Neutrons: 26 − 12 = 14 and 24 − 12 = 12; difference = 2.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of lithium (proton number 3)?

items.q: Why do <sup>39</sup><sub>19</sub>K and <sup>41</sup><sub>19</sub>K have the same chemical properties?

items.q: Silver-107 and silver-108 are isotopes. What do they have the same number of?

items.q: How many protons are in the ion Li<sup>+</sup>?

items.q: How many protons are in the ion Se<sup>2−</sup>?

items.q: An ion has 17 protons and 18 electrons. What is it?

items.q: Why do <sup>6</sup><sub>3</sub>Li and <sup>7</sup><sub>3</sub>Li have the same chemical properties?

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 1?

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 2?

items.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of helium-4?

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 4?

items.q: A neutral atom of phosphorus has a mass number of 31. How many electrons does it have?
items.e: In a neutral atom, electrons = protons = 15.

items.q: How many electrons are in the outer shell of a lithium atom (proton number 3)?

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 8?

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of neon-20?

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of bromine-80?
items.e: The atomic number (35) is the number of protons.

items.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of rubidium-86?

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of calcium (proton number 20)?
items.e: Fill the shells in order: 2 in the first, 8 in the second, 8 in the third. Calcium: 2, 8, 8, 2.
